findings.claim: The visit's hidden flag is kept when a queue is started again on the same collection page, so after the reader hides the visit-shown pane, pressing Play or choosing a row again leaves the pane hidden with the tree setting off.
findings.impact: A reader who hid the pane on the collection list and then presses Play gets playback with no queue pane visible. One press of the pane button brings it back. Minor and easy to recover from.
findings.evidence: TwoPaneLayout.tsx:151-152 calls show() only when the visit is not active ('A pane the reader hid stays hidden until the button asks for it'). useTreeVisible.ts:48-49 hides a visit with hidden=true. CollectionDetail's playFile does not touch treeVisitStore. I13 says 'starting a queue at md or wider shows its pane'.
findings.repro: not_reproduced (read only). Steps: tree:enabled:main=false, md+ width. Open /drive/main/collections/c1, press Play, press the collection name (?file= cleared, pane kept), press the pane button (pane hides, nothing written), press Play. The pane stays hidden.

bucket_proposal.reason: The visit was started earlier on this page, so this is arguably a continuation of the visit rather than a new start. The reader asked to hide the pane, which reads as deliberate, but whether a new Play should re-show it is a product decision.

findings.proposed_fix: Decide whether Play/row choice re-shows a hidden visit pane; if so, call treeVisitStore.show on a queue start.

specification_compliance: r8 F1 (I13/I18): fixed. useTreeVisible.ts:66-70 routes a press to treeVisitStore.toggle whenever a visit is active at md+ and the pane is not yielded, whether or not a file is open. On the collection list after ?file= is cleared, the button now hides and re-shows the kept pane without calling setEnabled, so tree:enabled is not written.

The precedence on a file page is unchanged: yielded → reopen first (I17/I18), then the visit toggle, then the setting table. Before the fix, a visit on a file page was also checked before `reopened`, so moving the branch up changes behaviour only where filePage is false.

Folder pages without a visit still reach `setEnabled(!enabled)` (useTreeVisible.ts:86-89), because visit.active is false there (TwoPaneLayout.tsx:143-150 clears it unless queuePane&&hasFile or visitUntilLeft has started).
Below md the visit is cleared (TwoPaneLayout.tsx:143-149), so phone presses still go to treeNarrowOpenStore (SPEC-CORE-193).

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: A visit-shown pane that the reader hid stays hidden when a queue is started again on the same collection page (Play or a row choice).
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: show() is skipped while the visit is active, so after hiding the pane on the list and pressing Play the pane remains hidden until the button is pressed.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: On a collection page with the tree setting off, opening any file (a grid card or link) starts the visit, and the item pane then stays on the collection list until the page is left.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: visitStarted is set by any queuePane && hasFile, so a card click leaves the pane shown on the list afterwards.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: Ending a folder queue removes `sort` and `order` even when they were the listing's own URL sort.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: After a URL-sorted listing, Play all and ×, the listing falls back to its stored sort.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: A visit-shown pane the reader hid comes back after the viewport crosses md and returns.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: Below md the visit is cleared, and above md show() starts it again with hidden=false.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: A play intent left pending by a selection that the navigation guard cancelled autoplays the next arrival at that file by any route.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: playIntent.ts holds the id until takePlayIntent matches it.

regression_risks: The visit toggle now precedes the filePage branch. On a file page with visit.active and yieldState.reopened, the press hides the visit pane rather than writing false. This was already the order before the fix, but it now applies to every state where visit is active.

shownBySetting (TwoPaneLayout.tsx:192) is true while a visit is active even when hidden. A yield is prevented only by the hidden pane's zero offsetWidth (useInspectorFit.ts:117); a measurement during the width transition could yield a pane the reader just hid, after which the first press only reopens and a second press shows it.
test_coverage: TwoPaneLayout.queuePane.test.tsx adds a case with visitUntilLeft: open a file, clear ?file=, press the real TreeToggle twice, and assert the pane hides and re-shows with tree:enabled:work never written. Reverting the fix (setEnabled path) would fail it, so it covers r8 F1/F2.
The new case runs TwoPaneLayout directly, not through CollectionDetail; CollectionDetail.queue.test.tsx still mocks TreeToggle to null.
No test covers Play after hiding the visit pane on the list (F1 of this round).
No test covers a press on a file page with visit.active and yieldState.reopened after the branch reorder.
not_verified: I did not run any test, build or browser; all claims come from reading.
I did not trace the yield measurement during the CSS width transition of a just-hidden pane (regression risk 2).
I did not re-read the players, RightPaneFile or the queue hosts beyond the diff for this round.
I did not verify I1 (watch record on end) in the player progress hooks.
trajectory: The r8 fix (fbec1054) adds no new state, prop or store. It moves the existing `visit.active` branch in useTreeVisible.toggle out of the `yieldState.filePage` block, puts it in front of that block with a `!yieldState.yielded` guard, and removes the inner `else if (visit.active)` arm. Net, this round relocates a branch and deletes one, rather than adding a branch on top of the previous round's. The earlier pattern still stands: r7's fixes added `replacesTrail`, `visitUntilLeft` with two refs, and `sidebarOverlay`, and r8's breach came from where the visit and yield/filePage states meet. This round closes that seam without adding to it. The tree-pane visibility still rests on four interacting stores (enabled, narrow-open, yield, visit), and the remaining low-impact behaviours (hidden visit kept across a new Play, re-shown after an md crossing) sit on the same visit/hidden state.
